title: History 11: Audio models: WaveNet to autoregressive music to diffusion music
hook: From one call per sample to one model call per step, then a model that does both. Where the time goes in each era.

verified.claim: WaveNet works on raw waveforms with at least 16,000 samples per second, predicts sequentially, and a dilation stack 1, 2, 4 ... 512 has a receptive field of 1024.
MusicGen is one transformer over EnCodec tokens: 32 kHz audio, a stride of 640, 50 Hz, with 4 codebooks.
The lab's dilated stack measured 1024 samples by autograd, matching the paper.
Music 3's AR stage runs 25 frames a second in ComfyUI, then a DiT runs on the result.
ACE-Step 1.5 has AceStepDiTModel, plus an AceStepAudioTokenizer using residual FSQ.
LTX's audio path has CausalAudioAutoencoder and a Vocoder.
The graph passes validate_prompt with file menus skipped.

unchecked: The call counts are simple counts. Time per call varies hugely between models. A diffusion call covers far more data, so fewer calls does not mean faster.
We did not read how ACE-Step uses its tokenizer during generation beyond what the class names and module docstrings show. The lesson says so where it matters.
WaveNet's count assumes one call per sample with no caching, which is what the paper's sequential description means. Later work sped this up, and we did not cover that.
The first version said NADiffusionDecoder is part of LTX 2.4's audio path. It's a video VAE decoder, per its file's first line, so that's removed.
